key_insight: For LPBF A20X, friction stir welding alone preserves corrosion resistance better than post-weld solution treatment and aging, which significantly worsens corrosion performance.
engineering_relevance: For aerospace-grade additively manufactured aluminum parts, weld and heat-treatment choices directly affect durability in chloride environments and must be jointly optimized.
method: Compared four conditions: BM, as-welded SZ, BM–PA, and SZ–PA.
Used electron microscopy and XRD to track microstructural changes.
Evaluated corrosion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl via EIS and potentiodynamic polarization.
evidence_signal: BM had the lowest corrosion current density (0.703 μA/cm2), while SZ–PA was highest (3.181 μA/cm2), with impedance and SEM confirming poorer resistance after aging.
watch_item: Results are specific to the tested LPBF A20X condition, welding setup, and NaCl exposure, so process-window changes may alter the corrosion ranking.
paper_title: Influence of Friction Stir Welding and Post-Weld Aging on Corrosion Behavior of LPBF A20X Alloy
